ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows two overlapping equilateral triangles forming a star-like outline. Inside them is a bold hexagon. The bold hexagon has a top horizontal side labeled 6, an upper-right slanted side labeled 15, a lower-right slanted side labeled 11, and a bottom horizontal side labeled 12. The two left slanted sides of the bold hexagon are not labeled. Reasoning: Let the two unknown left slanted side lengths be x and y. Since the outer shapes are equilateral triangles, all slanted sides make 60-degree angles with the horizontal, while the top and bottom sides of the hexagon are horizontal. Around the closed hexagon, the total vertical drop along the two right slanted sides must equal the total vertical rise along the two left slanted sides. Each slanted side has vertical component equal to its length times sin 60°, so (15 + 11)sin60° = (x + y)sin60°. Therefore x + y = 26. The perimeter is 6 + 15 + 11 + 12 + x + y = 6 + 15 + 11 + 12 + 26 = 70.

raw_record.question_text: Two equilateral triangles of different sizes are placed on top of each other so that a hexagon is formed on the inside whose opposite sides are parallel. Four of the side lengths of the hexagon are stated in the diagram. How big is the perimeter of the hexagon?

method.method_draft: First read the bold inner hexagon in the image: its labeled sides are top horizontal 6, upper-right slanted 15, lower-right slanted 11, and bottom horizontal 12; the two left slanted sides are unknown. Let those two unknown left slanted sides be x and y. Because the diagram is made from equilateral triangles, all slanted sides are at 60 degrees to the horizontal, and the top and bottom hexagon sides are horizontal. Moving around the closed hexagon, the total vertical drop along the two right slanted sides must equal the total vertical rise along the two left slanted sides. Since each slanted side has the same vertical scale factor sin 60°, this gives x + y = 15 + 11 = 26. Therefore the perimeter is 6 + 15 + 11 + 12 + 26 = 70.

method.method_draft: Label the inner hexagon clockwise as A B C D E F, with AB = 6, BC = 15, CD = 11, DE = 12, and unknowns EF = x and FA = y. Use the outer equilateral-triangle structure visible in the image: each side of the inner hexagon is the base of a small equilateral outer tip, so the exterior segments adjacent to a hexagon side have the same length as that side. Its right side is composed of an exterior segment equal to AB = 6, then BC = 15, then an exterior segment equal to CD = 11, so that side has length 6 + 15 + 11 = 32. Its left side is composed of 6 + y + x, and must also equal 32, so 6 + y + 9 = 32, giving y = 17. The perimeter is then 6 + 15 + 11 + 12 + 9 + 17 = 70.
